title: Senior's toolkit: running and inspecting Camel routes
summary: The Camel CLI (Camel JBang) commands for running a route in dev mode, seeing its state and following a message through it.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: running and inspecting Camel routes
steps.body: The Camel CLI (`camel`, installed with JBang) runs YAML routes without a project and lets you look inside a running integration. You use it to try a route in seconds and to see why a message went the wrong way.

toolkit.what: Creates a starter route file in the DSL the extension implies, so you begin from valid syntax.
Runs routes straight from source. With `--dev` it reloads when you save a file, so you edit and test in a loop.
flags: port for the embedded HTTP server (platform-http)
run every route file in a folder
name the integration for the other commands
toolkit.when: every time you write or change a route

toolkit.what: Lists the Camel integrations running on this machine, with their name, PID, age and status.
Shows every route of the running integrations: its id, `from` endpoint, status, and how many messages passed or failed.
flags: the health checks and their state
toolkit.when: "did my message even reach the route?"

toolkit.what: Follows the log of a running integration, without hunting for the file.
flags: only that integration; without it, the logs of all of them, each line prefixed with its name

toolkit.what: Prints each message as it passes every step of the route, with headers and body, so you see where a header changed or a branch was taken.
flags: start the integration with tracing on
toolkit.example: camel run orders.camel.yaml --dev --trace   # then, in another terminal: camel trace orders

toolkit.what: Turns the routes you ran with the CLI into a real Maven project for production (Quarkus, Spring Boot or Camel Main).
Stops a running integration cleanly by name.

steps.prompt: Match each command to the job.
pairs: run routes and reload them when you save
see message counts and failures per route
follow one message through every step
turn the routes into a project for production

steps.prompt: You POST an order to `http://localhost:8080/orders` and get a 200 back, but the warehouse never sees it. `camel get route` shows `orders-in` with `Total 1, Failed 0` and `to-warehouse` with `Total 0`. What is the best next step?
options: Run with `--trace` and use `camel trace` to see which branch the message took and what its headers were
steps.explain: The message arrived and nothing failed, so it went somewhere else: a `choice` that took `otherwise`, a filter that dropped it, or a header that changed the target. A trace shows the path and the headers at each step.

steps.prompt: Run every route in `routes/` as the integration `orders` on port 8080, reloading on save.
steps.explain: `--source-dir` runs every route file in the folder; `--dev` reloads when a file changes. `--trace` is real but traces messages; it does not reload.

steps.prompt: A route calls a backend with `to: http://...`. The backend logs show strange headers such as `CamelHttpUri` and the client's `Authorization` arriving. Which command shows you, step by step, which headers the message carried when it left Camel?
steps.explain: A trace records headers and body at each step, so you see the client's headers riding along to the `to:`. The fix is the header gotcha from this module: `removeHeaders` before calling out.

steps.prompt: Put a route change in order, from first try to production.
lines: Send a test request with curl and check `camel get route`
Trace one message with `camel trace` if it went the wrong way
Commit the project and let the pipeline build and deploy it

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Try every route change with `camel run --dev` and a curl before it goes near a pipeline. When a message goes missing, read `camel get route` for the counts first and turn on tracing second; guessing from the YAML alone wastes an afternoon.
